Part 1: https://youtu.be/TDLdNXU7hqY
--------
In this VladTV interview, John Franzese Jr. explains what happened immediately after he testified against his own father and entered the U.S. Marshals Witness Protection Program. Franzese says officials took and destroyed his phone, then struggled to place him safely because of his family’s wide-reaching Mafia connections, from New York ties to people as far away as Montana, comparing the challenge to cases involving Sammy “The Bull” Gravano. He describes temporary relocations, a first permanent stop in South Carolina, a security scare involving someone with gang ties, a brief move through North Carolina, and finally settling in Indianapolis under the name Matt Passerelle. Franzese also addresses a key misconception: he says he was not facing charges or cooperating to avoid prison time. Instead, he says he had become repulsed by the life and wanted out. The conversation covers loyalty, informants, family betrayal, and leaving organized crime.

--------
Former Hells Angels enforcer George “Joby” Walters sits down with VladTV to trace the road that led him from a troubled childhood in southeastern Ohio to the ranks of the Avengers Motorcycle Club. Walters opens up about growing up around alcoholism and violence, joining the Army at 17, serving with the 101st Airborne at Fort Campbell and traveling Europe on a Norton Commando before returning home restless for the biker life.

He recalls meeting Avengers MC members in Huntington, West Virginia, after bike trouble, including Mike “Frick” Forbush and state president Big Dave. Walters explains how he became a prospect, earned his patch, and was made warlord for the charter within months. The conversation also covers 1%er motorcycle club culture in the 1980s, tensions with the Outlaws and Pagans, and a serious crash involving a pickup truck in Huntington. Sonny Barger, Hells Angels history, and the River Run riot frame this candid interview.

--------
Jimmy DiModica sits down with Vlad to discuss his time around the Gambino crime family, taking control of a union, and the realities of “kicking up” money to figures like Jackie D’Amico. DiModica explains his philosophy of sharing profits, his memories of John Gotti’s circle, and how mob politics shaped his path in the early 2000s.

The conversation also revisits one of DiModica’s most unusual stories: studying Lawrence Revere’s *Playing Blackjack as a Business*, applying card counting in Atlantic City, and winning $386,000 on Halloween night in 1983 before being banned from the casinos. He reflects on going “full throttle” when learning a skill, the consequences of his lifestyle, and how the death of his sponsor, “Little Sammy,” may have changed his future.

Topics include the Gambino family, Atlantic City blackjack, card counting, John Gotti, Jackie D’Amico, union control, and federal prison time.

--------
In this VladTV interview, Rainwater gives a detailed account of Mo3’s final days and the phone call he says he was on when the Dallas rapper was shot on November 11, 2020. He reflects on Mo3’s rising momentum after working with Boosie Badazz on their joint project, the visibility that followed, and plans that included a possible Vlad interview and the film “Triple D Revenge.” Rainwater also discusses Mo3’s trip back from California, meetings involving Black Youngsta and Gotti, and the moments leading up to the tragedy. He recalls hearing Mo3 say people were shooting at him, staying on the line as first responders arrived, and contacting Mo3’s brother for help. A sober look at Mo3’s career, relationships, and the impact of his death on Dallas hip-hop.

--------
Former DEA agent Chris Feistl sits down with Vlad to reflect on his role in taking down the Cali Cartel and consulting on Netflix’s *Narcos* Season 3. Feistl discusses being portrayed by Michael Stahl-David, working with the show after the success of Javier Peña and Steve Murphy’s storylines, and what the series got right about Colombia’s drug war after Pablo Escobar.

The conversation expands into today’s cocaine trade, from increased coca production in Colombia to Mexico tunnels, corruption, money laundering, arms trafficking, and the challenges facing U.S. law enforcement. Feistl explains why, even with unlimited DEA resources, stopping cocaine from entering America may be impossible.

He also weighs in on marijuana legalization, the debate over legalizing cocaine, crack cocaine concerns, and the ongoing public health and crime impacts. Feistl closes by discussing his book *After Escobar*, co-written with Dave Mitchell and Jessica Boni.
